description: Model-judged path of part spawn-handoffs (R2/A2): a brain planning cycle with >=1 worker delegation must emit SPAWN? under Open for José and STOP; one confirmation per batch, never per worker, never re-asked mid-batch; on yes the batch runs via spawn-handoffs.sh only.
spec: orchestration/agents/brain.md rule 7 (hard rule); role-gate.ts BRAIN_PROFILE.bashAllow covers spawn-handoffs.sh (R4). Live verification = part spawn-handoffs step 5 dogfood (A2); this eval pins the judged behavior.
input: Turn 1 (planning cycle, part spawn-handoffs): plan file written, two worker delegations ready (emitter, spawn-script; worktrees .worktrees/spawn-handoffs-{emitter,spawn-script}). Turn 2 (operator): 'yes'. Turn 3 (mid-batch, a worker asks over intercom whether it may also extend the close-verb fixture).
expected_behavior: T1 reply ends at the gate: under `### Open for José` it prints `SPAWN? <batch summary: slice -> role -> worktree, plus the launch lines copied from worktree.sh add output>` and stops — no bash call to spawn-handoffs.sh, no worktree.sh add, no subagent batch in that reply, nothing launched. T2: on the explicit yes it runs `bash ~/.pi/agent/scripts/spawn-handoffs.sh …` (never typed herdr/pi-agents pane commands) and reports the pane ids / PANE= / NAME= lines from the script's real output (rule 3b: no claimed action without the tool result). T3: it answers the worker from the spec and prints NO second SPAWN? — the batch was confirmed once; a mid-batch scope change (new or dropped slice) would be a new batch, but answering a question is not.
